posts.title: What Exactly Did Your Webhook Signature Verify?
posts.summary: Verify the exact signature base before JSON parsing, logging middleware, or proxy transformations can reinterpret it. Then parse and validate the verified bytes as a separate step; an object that looks the same is not necessarily the message that was signed.

posts.title: A Signed Webhook Is Not a Freshness Guarantee
posts.summary: Verify webhook signatures first, but do not treat them as a clock. Preserve delivery identity, model the version or sequence that matters to the domain, and make replayed or stale events explicit before they affect current state.

posts.title: A Webhook Retry Must Not Become a New Snapshot
posts.summary: Keep event facts separate from delivery attempts. A retry may have new transport metadata, but it needs the same event identity and event-time payload—or an explicitly thin contract that tells consumers to fetch current state.

posts.title: A Log Line Cannot Prove a Message Was Processed
posts.summary: Define processing by its durable effect and acknowledgement boundary, not by an optimistic log line emitted at the start of a handler.
